messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: GPU pool saturation detected in us-west-2: gpu-pool-3. autoscaler attempted 3x scale but hit provider quota, queue length rising >1200, request throttle ratio 32%. Root hint: model:v30.2 serving traffic spike.
sarah (oncall): I'm on it. joining bridge. grabbing logs and checking which model versions are hot.
jordan (ml): ping — we just rolled v30.2 at 00:08 UTC to reduce hallucinations. it has a new context-span optimization that keeps more KV in memory; might increase per-request GPU memory.
sarah (oncall): copying. current tail latencies show 95p -> 2.8s, 99p -> 9.2s. 503s creeping up. which pools serving v30.2?
lee (runtime): gpu-pool-3 and gpu-pool-4 taking most of v30.2 traffic. autoscaler logs show repeated OOM prevention and then provider denied scale: "quota_exceeded". our autoscale policy capped at 24 nodes, target would be 40.
devin (support): any customer-facing impact flags? I'm seeing increased errors for a handful of midmarket tenants — elevated request failures and slower responses.
sarah (oncall): marking SEV-2 for now. bridge link: https://bridge.company/redwood/4912345678
jordan (ml): quick config note: v30.2 default context_window set to 16384 vs 8192 in v30.1. we turned on KV aggressive retention. that will increase GPU mem per session. i can push a model config tweak to reduce retention window to 12k if we want to try a softer approach.
lee (runtime): two immediate mitigations: 1) pause rollout of v30.2 (stop new nodes routing to that variant). 2) enable fallback routing to v29.4 for heavy requests. both low-risk.
sarah (oncall): do it. lee, can you pause rollout? jordan, can you start config tweak as parallel plan?
lee (runtime): pausing rollout now. command: ```sh
# pause traffic to v30.2
redwoodctl rollout pause --model v30.2 --region us-west-2
```
ops-bot: Action accepted: rollout v30.2 traffic paused by lee at 4912345690. current traffic shifting to stable variants.
lee (runtime): switching heavy-request routing to v29.4 canary. applying routing override: ```json
{"policy": "route_by_size", "threshold": 4000}
```
sarah (oncall): traffic shift looks good, queues decreased from 1200 -> 780 in last 2m. still high but trending.
jordan (ml): started a quick config patch to set context_window=12288 and reduce kv_retention to moderate. patch id: cfg-3492. if applied, expected mem reduction ~18-25% per session.
lee (runtime): can't rely solely on model tune. autoscaler still blocked by provider quota. requesting manual scale request with provider: open ticket and try hot spare addon. nathan, can you spin up reserved instances or request quota bump?
nathan (prod-eng): already on provider chat. requesting immediate quota bump; meanwhile provisioning preemptible auxiliary GPUs in eu-west as emergency overlay not ideal but possible. ETA ~12m for new capacity.
devin (support): notifying affected accounts: sending templated message indicating elevated latency and we're actively mitigating. Will do not to promise ETA.
sarah (oncall): for immediate relief, enable prefilling throttles for large-context prefills. runtime flag: prefill.max_concurrency=8 for v30.* in us-west-2. lee, can you flip that?
lee (runtime): flipping prefill throttle now. ```sh
redwoodctl config set runtime.prefill.max_concurrency=8 --selector region=us-west-2,model=v30*
```
ops-bot: Config update applied. Note: risk of increased tail latency for small requests while throttles apply.
sarah (oncall): observed queue drop to 420 after routing + throttle. error rate stabilizing. good sign.
jordan (ml): cfg-3492 applied to green canary now. monitors show memory per session down 20% on sample hosts. preparing to roll patch and revert context_window in 5m if stable.
lee (runtime): manual scaling request accepted by provider for +8 GPUs in us-west-2. provisioning started. node init logs: "kubelet: node registered" at 4912345708.
sarah (oncall): oncall handoff: i'm staying on until we confirm stable. nathan and jordan, if provider nodes land, we should let autoscaler settle then re-evaluate rollback vs gradual rollout.
devin (support): customer comms updated: "We've deployed mitigations to reduce latency and are monitoring. Some requests may have experienced delays between 00:05–00:25 UTC. No data loss. We'll share a follow-up soon."
lee (runtime): follow-up actions: 1) keep v30.2 paused, 2) apply cfg-3492 globally after validation, 3) request quota bump permanently, 4) add autoscaler safety guard to prevent too-fast scaling when provider returns quota_exceeded (to avoid thrash).
jordan (ml): agreed. i'm going to revert context_window to 8192 on stable track and create a night-run experiment for 16k windows with KV retention limits.
sarah (oncall): summary for now: GPUs saturated due to v30.2 config change increasing per-session GPU memory and a prefill wave. Autoscaler attempted to scale but hit provider quota leading to queue growth and throttling. Mitigations: paused rollout, routed heavy requests to v29.4, applied prefill throttle, deployed model config patch reducing mem, manual provider scale. Customer impact: elevated latency and increased errors for a subset of tenants, window ~00:05–00:25 UTC, no data loss, degraded but operational.
ops-bot: Incident severity set to SEV-2 by sarah (oncall).
lee (runtime): postmortem owners: lee, jordan, nathan. I'll open a postmortem draft and include timeline + mitigation commands.
sarah (oncall): thanks team. i'll update the incident page and schedule a follow-up review. staying on until 00:45 UTC then hand off to nathan.
nathan (prod-eng): taking handoff at 00:45. will monitor for 1 hour and coordinate long-term fixes (quota bump, autoscaler policy change, model rollout checklist).
devin (support): recording affected customer list and next steps for outbound comms.
sarah (oncall): closing bridge in 5. good work. :white_check_mark:
